fixes.explanation: Right, baker. They picture Egypt as a place "…where we will not see war or hear the sound of the ram’s horn or hunger for bread…" War and hunger are the two things they say they won't face there. That's the picture they paint in the LORD's second if.

Makes sense, friend, with Gedaliah, the governor Babylon appointed (Jeremiah 40:5), gone (Jeremiah 41:2). But the people don't ask for a new governor. They ask Jeremiah to pray that the LORD will tell them "…the way we should walk and the thing we should do." They want a direction for their feet.

I see why you'd go there, since Ishmael son of Nethaniah, who struck down Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:2), was just in the story. But the people don't mention him here. They say obeying is "…so that it may go well with us…" It's the whole picture they have in mind, not just one man.

I can see how you landed there, since folks are scared. But the LORD doesn't say hide. He says, "If you will indeed stay in this land, then I will build you up and not tear you down…" The word He uses is stay.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear…" He says it twice in a row. When God repeats Himself, I lean in.
Jealous isn't the word here, baker. The LORD says, "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear…" He names fear, plain and simple.
Not Moab, friend. The LORD names a different land. He pictures them saying, "…we will go to the land of Egypt and live there…"
Edom isn't the one here, baker. The LORD names a different land. The second if has them saying, "No, but we will go to the land of Egypt and live there…" Egypt is the answer.
That's it, baker. The LORD says "…the sword you fear will overtake you there, and the famine you dread will follow on your heels into Egypt…" The very things they fear and dread come along with them.
Not Babylon, friend. The LORD doesn't name it in that line. He says, "…you will never see this place again." That place is the land they're in now.
Good thinking, friend, but the Nile isn't mentioned in this passage. The LORD says, "…you will never see this place again." He's talking about the land they're in now.

Right, baker. Jeremiah says, "…you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in all He has sent me to tell you." He's not praising them, he's pointing out they haven't done it. It's a hard thing to hear.
